resources.name: 988 Colorado Mental Health Line
resources.intake: Call or text 988 for immediate support.
resources.eligibility: Open to anyone in Colorado experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis
resources.services: Free, confidential statewide mental health, emotional distress, and substance use support.
resources.notes: For in-person crisis care in Denver, visit WellPower’s 24/7 Walk-In Crisis Center at 4353 E. Colfax Ave. No appointment or insurance is required. [WellPower walk-in crisis services](https://www.wellpower.org/crisis-services/) Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.988colorado.com/en/colorado-crisis-services

resources.name: Denver Health Emergency Psychiatric Services
resources.intake: Walk in through the Emergency Department entrance at Pavilion A, off the Delaware Street circle drive. Call the 24-hour NurseLine if unsure where to seek care.
resources.eligibility: Adults and youth experiencing a psychiatric emergency. The emergency department directs patients to the appropriate team.
resources.services: Crisis stabilization, evaluation, treatment
resources.notes: The listed phone is the Denver Health NurseLine. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denverhealth.org/services/behavioral-and-mental-health-services/emergency-services

resources.name: Support Team Assisted Response (STAR)
resources.hours: STAR field response: daily 6 AM–10 PM per City of Denver.
resources.intake: In Denver, call 720-913-7827 or 911 and ask about STAR. Dispatch determines the appropriate available response. For a life-threatening emergency, call 911.
resources.eligibility: Low-risk calls in Denver involving mental health distress or substance use, without significant safety concerns.
resources.services: Mobile response by a behavioral health clinician and paramedic.
resources.notes: Dispatch-based service. Denver publishes daily response hours. A partner’s page lists weekday coverage, so use dispatch to confirm availability. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Public-Health-Environment/Community-Behavioral-Health/Behavioral-Health-Support/Behavioral-Health-Outreach/Support-Team-Assisted-Response-STAR-Program

resources.name: WellPower – Outpatient Mental Health Intake
resources.intake: Call 303-504-7700 or request a callback at https://www.wellpower.org/appointment/ to start services. Confirm the assigned clinic before going.
resources.eligibility: Individuals seeking mental health care
resources.services: Mental health therapy, psychiatric services
resources.notes: Outpatient intake line. For in-person crisis support, WellPower’s separate walk-in center is open 24/7 at 4353 E. Colfax Ave. [WellPower walk-in crisis services](https://www.wellpower.org/crisis-services/) Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.wellpower.org/contact/

resources.name: Youth Seen
resources.hours: By appointment. Call or text to arrange a consultation.
resources.intake: Call or text 720-788-0451 to request a consultation. Confirm whether your appointment is in person or remote.
resources.eligibility: LGBTQI+ youth and families. Ask about availability and fit.
resources.services: Mental health counseling, family counseling, gender-affirming support, and peer mentoring.
resources.notes: Use the counseling contact to confirm appointment details. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://youthseen.org/counseling-services/

resources.name: RMHS – Mission Supports
resources.hours: Contact the program for intake availability.
resources.intake: Submit the online referral form on the program page. Call 303-636-5782 or email missionsupports@rmhumanservices.org with questions.
resources.eligibility: People of any age who live in or plan to live in Denver County, face housing instability, and have a suspected or documented developmental disability and want a formal determination.
resources.services: Short-term case management, disability determination and benefits navigation, and connections to longer-term supports.
resources.notes: Use the program referral form to start services. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.rmhumanservices.org/departments/mission-supports/

resources.name: Rocky Mountain Human Services – General Program Intake
resources.intake: Call 303-636-5600 to identify the right program or locate an assigned case manager.
resources.eligibility: Varies by program. Ask about eligibility and service area.
resources.services: Early intervention for children, behavioral health support, case management for I/DD, veteran housing and health services
resources.notes: General intake and routing. For housing instability and developmental disability determination in Denver County, see RMHS – Mission Supports. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.rmhumanservices.org/contact-us/

resources.name: Servicios de La Raza – Re-Entry Program
resources.hours: Program intake by arrangement. Peer group schedules vary.
resources.intake: Call 303-458-5851 and ask for Re-Entry to confirm enrollment and referral requirements. Check the program page for peer group times and locations.
resources.eligibility: People preparing for release or returning to the community after incarceration. Confirm program-specific enrollment requirements.
resources.services: Re-entry support with documents, housing, transportation, employment resources, and peer groups.
resources.notes: The provider lists different locations for support groups. Check the program page before attending. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://serviciosdelaraza.org/re-entry-program/

resources.name: A Precious Child
resources.intake: Get a referral through a partner agency, then schedule a Resource Center shopping appointment. Call 303-466-4272, option 2, with questions.
resources.eligibility: Must meet federal poverty line or qualify for government assistance
resources.services: Clothing, emergency family assistance
resources.notes: Referral and appointment are required before visiting the Broomfield Resource Center. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://apreciouschild.org/about-us/receive-support/

resources.name: Bridget's Boutique at The Gathering Place
resources.hours: Ask the Resource Desk for current boutique appointments.
resources.intake: Members should ask the Resource Desk to book a Bridget’s Boutique appointment.
resources.eligibility: Members of The Gathering Place. Ask the Resource Desk about clothing access for your household.
resources.services: Seasonal clothing, casual attire
resources.notes: Clothing bank access is by appointment. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://tgpdenver.org/what-we-do/programs-services.html

resources.name: Clothes to Kids of Denver
resources.hours: By appointment. Ask about pickup availability.
resources.intake: Call 720-379-4630 or email appointment@clothestokidsdenver.org to schedule shopping or ask about curbside pickup.
resources.eligibility: Eligible school-aged students in the Denver area. Review the provider’s eligibility criteria, including for students experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Complete wardrobe for students
resources.notes: Confirm student eligibility and appointment before traveling. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://clothestokidsdenver.org/referral-process/

resources.name: Dress for Success
resources.intake: Ask an approved referral agency to arrange a suiting appointment. Call 303-832-1889 with suiting questions.
resources.eligibility: Women seeking employment
resources.services: Interview clothing and apparel for women entering the workforce.
resources.notes: This clothing listing is for the Suiting program. Career services have a separate Employment & Workforce Development entry. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://denver.dressforsuccess.org/programs/suiting/

resources.name: The Action Center – Clothing Market
resources.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9–11:30 AM and 1–3:30 PM. Check closures.
resources.intake: Walk in. No appointment needed. Eligible households may shop up to twice per month within their point allowance.
resources.eligibility: No appointment or referral necessary
resources.services: Free gently used clothing, shoes, and accessories.
resources.notes: Clothing Market address and hours differ from some other Action Center services. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.theactioncenter.org/clothing-bank

resources.name: The Salvation Army Denver Citadel Corps
resources.intake: Call 303-922-4549 to confirm food pantry access and the hours for the service you need.
resources.eligibility: Open to all; some services require appointments
resources.services: Food pantry and community center programs.
resources.notes: For utility assistance use the separate Salvation Army Family Services listing. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://denvercitadel.salvationarmy.org/

resources.name: BirdSeed Collective
resources.intake: Check BirdSeed’s current distribution location and schedule before going. The organization announced a move from the former Globeville Center location.
resources.eligibility: Open to all community members
resources.services: Free healthy food distribution, art and music classes, athletic and recreational activities, cultural and educational programs, community events and meetings
resources.notes: Former Grant Street address removed because the provider announced an interim location and still displays legacy program details. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.birdseedcollective.org/globeville-center

resources.name: Denver Dream Center
resources.intake: Call 720-510-9113 to ask about Dream Closet & Pantry screening, pickup or delivery arrangements, and current availability.
resources.eligibility: Open to individuals experiencing homelessness, poverty, addiction, or reentry challenges
resources.services: Food, clothing, household essentials, and possible beds or furniture for families in crisis.
resources.notes: Arrange access with the program before visiting. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denverdreamcenter.org/programs/dream-closet-pantry

resources.name: EarthLinks
resources.intake: Call 303-389-0085 or ask at 2746 W. 13th Ave. for Workshop Program application instructions.
resources.eligibility: Individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness
resources.services: Organic gardening, eco-product workshops, case management, nature trips, community support
resources.notes: Provider lists limited Workshop Program capacity. The retail storefront has separate access. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.earthlinks-colorado.org/become-a-participant

resources.name: Holy Ghost Catholic Church
resources.hours: Call Social Ministry to confirm service hours.
resources.intake: Call the Social Ministry office about sandwich service and current intake before visiting.
resources.eligibility: No restrictions
resources.services: Hygiene products (when available)
resources.notes: The parish has published a sandwich line. Confirm the current schedule directly. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://holyghostchurch.org/about-us/staff/

resources.name: Southwest Improvement Council (SWIC)
resources.intake: Contact SWIC about its older adult or homeownership programs and confirm the appropriate intake route.
resources.eligibility: Primarily for Southwest Denver residents
resources.services: Older adult services and homeownership education or navigation.
resources.notes: Ask about specific workshops, service area, and appointments. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://swic-denver.org/

resources.name: Metro Denver Homeless Initiative – OneHome Coordinated Entry
resources.intake: Ask your case manager or outreach worker for a OneHome assessment, or use MDHI’s access point list to find a participating site.
resources.eligibility: People experiencing homelessness in metro Denver.
resources.services: Coordinated Entry assessment and housing referrals when matched. An assessment does not guarantee placement.
resources.notes: Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.mdhi.org/need-help

resources.name: The Center for Trauma and Resilience
resources.hours: Contact the helpline for service availability.
resources.intake: Call 303-894-8000 for English or 303-718-8289 for Spanish to request trauma services and advocacy.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of crime seeking support.
resources.services: Trauma support, victim advocacy, and resource navigation.
resources.notes: Call for service location and intake details. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.traumahealth.org/trauma-services

resources.name: Aurora Regional Navigation Campus – Drop-In Day Center
resources.hours: Call Advance Pathways for current day-center hours.
resources.intake: Use the drop-in day center at 15500 E. 40th Ave. Call 303-343-7808 to confirm hours and access.
resources.eligibility: Adults experiencing homelessness in Aurora and the surrounding region.
resources.services: Drop-in day center with meals and supportive services.
resources.notes: Walk-in access at the former 19th Place site remains unverified. Campus location verified with the City of Aurora on 2026-11-23.

resources.name: Haven of Hope Jay Gould Center
resources.intake: Walk-in
resources.eligibility: No restrictions
resources.services: Private showers, hygiene kits, laundry services
resources.notes: Provides additional daytime shelter services. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.thoh.org/services-calendar Ask staff about mail and document safekeeping.

resources.name: Lawrence Street Community Center
resources.intake: Walk in for Denver Rescue Mission bed assignment. Access for people seeking shelter and dinner starts at 2:30 PM; arrive before 6 PM for transport to other sites. Breakfast and lunch access depends on prior overnight stay. Guests seeking a bed at the 48th Avenue Center must first sign up for bed assignment at this Lawrence Street location.
resources.eligibility: Open to individuals experiencing homelessness
resources.services: Day shelter, meals, restrooms, drinking water, bed assignments, referrals to services
resources.notes: Operated by Denver Rescue Mission; central hub for daytime support and services Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Department-of-Housing-Stability/Resident-Resources/Find-Shelter/Walk-Up-Shelter Denver Rescue Mission bed assignment instructions: [Denver Rescue Mission bed assignment instructions](https://denverrescuemission.org/get-help/inquiry/)

resources.name: Network Coffee House
resources.hours: Sun 11 AM–2 PM; Mon–Wed 10 AM–2 PM and 6–9 PM; Thu 10 AM–2 PM; Fri 6–9 PM; Sat 5:30–9 AM
resources.intake: Walk-in
resources.eligibility: Open to all seeking hospitality and companionship
resources.services: Drop-in hospitality and companionship for unhoused neighbors.
resources.notes: Focuses on affirming dignity and fostering kinship among unhoused neighbors Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.networkcoffeehouse.org/

resources.name: St. Francis Center
resources.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 7 AM–3 PM; Wed 7 AM–1 PM (noon close third Wed); Sat–Sun 7 AM–2 PM
resources.intake: Walk-in
resources.eligibility: No restrictions
resources.services: Showers (soap, shampoo, and towels provided)
resources.notes: Check provider page for service-specific hours. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.sfcdenver.org/programs-services/day-services/ The St. Francis Center Outreach team serves people experiencing unsheltered homelessness in downtown Denver and helps with identity documents and benefits, including SNAP, Medicaid, and Social Security. Outreach program details: [St. Francis Center outreach program](https://www.sfcdenver.org/programs-services/outreach/)

resources.name: The Gathering Place
resources.hours: Mon, Wed–Fri 8 AM–4 PM; Tue 8 AM–1:30 PM
resources.intake: Drop in during open hours. No ID or intake appointment required.
resources.eligibility: Women, gender-diverse people, and children facing homelessness or instability.
resources.services: Meals, showers, laundry, clothing bank, family services, case management, health services
resources.notes: Daytime drop-in center focused on women and transgender individuals experiencing poverty or homelessness. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://tgpdenver.org/what-we-do/if-you-need-help.html Members can ask about mail service and locker storage.

resources.name: Denver Youth Dental and Vision
resources.hours: Mon–Thu 9 AM–6 PM; Fri 8 AM–5 PM; Sat 8 AM–noon.
resources.intake: Call or book online for the Grove Street dental clinic. Call to confirm same-day availability and coverage.
resources.eligibility: Accepts Medicaid, CHP+, and major insurance
resources.services: Eye exams, glasses, contact lenses
resources.notes: The provider lists Medicaid acceptance and Spanish-speaking staff. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://denveryouthdentistry.com/locations/

resources.name: Kids in Need of Dentistry (KIND)
resources.intake: Complete the KIND eligibility application or call 720-619-5333 to request one. Confirm which clinic to visit after screening.
resources.eligibility: Children up to age 18 whose household meets KIND’s low-income guidelines.
resources.services: Cleanings, exams, fillings, orthodontics
resources.notes: Appointment location is assigned through KIND. Check which documents are needed to establish eligibility. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://kindsmiles.org/about/clinical-services/

resources.name: Stout Street Health Center Dental Clinic
resources.hours: Call to confirm site-specific dental hours.
resources.intake: New patients should use the Integrated Case Management intake link on the Coalition’s health locations page. Dental availability is limited. Established patients can call 303-293-2220 about appointments or walk-ins and confirm the assigned site.
resources.eligibility: Individuals experiencing homelessness
resources.services: General and emergency dental care
resources.notes: Coalition dental services are available at Stout Street Health Center and 2111 Champa St. Intake details: [Coalition dental intake details](https://coloradocoalition.org/healthlocations) Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.coloradocoalition.org/healthservices

resources.name: CU Anschutz Dental Clinics
resources.intake: Call 303-724-6900 to schedule a free screening and X-rays to be matched to a clinic. For urgent dental concerns, ask about the Dental First Aid Clinic.
resources.eligibility: Open to the public
resources.services: Cleanings, exams, emergency care, adolescent dental care
resources.notes: The free screening is the entry point. Ask about treatment costs, eligibility, and urgent appointment availability. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://dental.cuanschutz.edu/patient-care Urgent dental concerns: see the Dental First Aid Clinic for appointment instructions: [CU Anschutz Dental First Aid Clinic](https://dental.cuanschutz.edu/patient-care/our-clinics/dental-first-aid-clinic)

resources.name: DOVE (Deaf Overcoming Violence Through Empowerment)
resources.intake: Call the 24/7 hotline by videophone or voice. Voice callers connect through Video Relay Service. For routine inquiries, use the provider contact page.
resources.eligibility: Deaf, DeafBlind, DeafDisabled, and hard-of-hearing survivors seeking support.
resources.services: Advocacy, crisis support, safety planning, legal & medical assistance
resources.notes: Contact an advocate before visiting. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://deafdove.org/contact-us/

resources.name: Family Tree - Roots of Courage
resources.intake: Call for confidential shelter screening, safety planning, or advocacy.
resources.eligibility: People actively fleeing domestic violence seeking a safe place.
resources.services: Shelter, advocacy, crisis intervention, case management
resources.notes: Shelter location is confidential. Arrange access through the crisis line. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://thefamilytree.org/roots-of-courage/

resources.name: Three Birds Alliance (formerly Gateway Domestic Violence Services)
resources.intake: Call the crisis hotline for shelter screening and safety resources. Ask about pet accommodations if needed.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence
resources.services: Domestic violence shelter, advocacy, and support for survivors, families, and their pets.
resources.notes: Use the hotline to arrange shelter access. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://threebirdsalliance.org/contact/

resources.name: Rose Andom Center
resources.hours: Mon–Thu 9 AM–5 PM (last walk-in 4 PM); Fri 9 AM–noon (last walk-in 11 AM).
resources.intake: Call 720-337-4400 or walk in before the daily cutoff at 1330 Fox St.
resources.eligibility: Victims of domestic violence
resources.services: Coordinated services for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.
resources.notes: Check the provider page for closures and after-hours resources. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://roseandomcenter.org/

resources.name: SafeHouse Denver – Emergency Shelter and Crisis Line
resources.intake: Call 303-318-9989 for crisis support and confidential emergency shelter screening.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence
resources.services: Shelter, counseling, crisis intervention
resources.notes: Shelter address is confidential. Arrange shelter access through the crisis line. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.safehouse-denver.org/services/ Current SafeHouse clients can ask their advocate about the Extended Stay Program for additional time to secure housing.

resources.name: Emily Griffith Technical College
resources.intake: Use the admissions page for technical programs or call 720-423-4700. Ask directly whether high school equivalency preparation is currently enrolling.
resources.eligibility: 21+ for general GED, 17-20 for GED Plus
resources.services: GED classes, post-secondary transition support
resources.notes: The old GED classes link returned 404. Current GED preparation intake was not confirmed. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.emilygriffith.edu/admissions-steps/

resources.name: Mi Casa Resource Center
resources.intake: Choose a career pathway and submit its interest form. For admissions questions, call 303-539-5698. English and Spanish assistance available.
resources.eligibility: Open to adults and youth seeking career development
resources.services: Business coaching, job training, employment pathways
resources.notes: Screening, schedules, and training format vary by program. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://micasaresourcecenter.org/careerpathways/

resources.name: The Learning Source
resources.intake: Use the provider site or email info@thelearningsource.org to find a current GED or English class and confirm enrollment and location.
resources.eligibility: 17+, no ID required
resources.services: GED prep, ESL classes, college transition support
resources.notes: Programs run at multiple sites. Confirm the assigned class location. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://thelearningsource.org/how-we-help/

resources.name: Urban Peak Education Program
resources.intake: Call Urban Peak and ask how to connect with education support, GED preparation, or school re-enrollment.
resources.eligibility: Youth experiencing homelessness. Ask Urban Peak about age and enrollment requirements for specific education services.
resources.services: GED prep, re-engagement in high school, post-secondary guidance
resources.notes: Education assistance is part of Urban Peak’s youth support services. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.urbanpeak.org/services

resources.name: Denver Rescue Mission – Lawrence Street Shelter
resources.intake: Sign up for a bed assignment at Lawrence Street Community Center, 2222 Lawrence St. For afternoon shelter access, arrive from 2:30 PM and before 6 PM if transport is needed.
resources.eligibility: Men experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Emergency shelter, meals, faith-based support
resources.notes: Faith-based organization, supports long-term recovery. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Department-of-Housing-Stability/Resident-Resources/Find-Shelter/Walk-Up-Shelter

resources.name: The Delores Project
resources.intake: Call 303-534-5411 at 10 AM daily for bed availability and phone screening. Phone intake only. Walk-ups and agency referrals are unavailable.
resources.eligibility: Women, transgender, and nonbinary individuals experiencing homelessness
resources.services: Emergency shelter, supportive housing, rehousing assistance, behavioral health and wellness services
resources.notes: Focused on providing safe, dignified, and community-oriented shelter and housing solutions Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://thedeloresproject.org/need-shelter/

resources.name: The Salvation Army Crossroads Center
resources.hours: Shelter: 24/7; Office Hours: Mon - Fri 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM
resources.intake: Arrive at 10 AM daily for first-come, first-served intake, subject to bed availability. Call to confirm before arriving later.
resources.eligibility: Men and people who identify as male, age 18+, experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Emergency shelter, meals, case management, laundry, showers, hygiene items
resources.notes: Client-centered and trauma-informed care for men experiencing homelessness in Denver Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Department-of-Housing-Stability/Resident-Resources/Find-Shelter/Walk-Up-Shelter

resources.name: Salvation Army Connection Center – Family Shelter Intake
resources.intake: Call 303-295-3366 for family shelter screening, referral, and availability.
resources.eligibility: Families with minor children seeking shelter.
resources.services: Phone screening and referrals to family shelters.
resources.notes: Phone referral service. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://westernusa.salvationarmy.org/im-connection-center/

resources.name: Sinton's Sanctuary
resources.intake: A community agency must submit a referral form. Call 720-234-5195 for program information.
resources.eligibility: Women 55 and older experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Shelter, meals, showers, case management, transition to permanent housing
resources.notes: 24-hour shelter and support services for eligible guests. Online source checked 2026-11-23: https://www.voacolorado.org/locations/sintons-sanctuary/

resources.name: Dress for Success
resources.intake: Ask a listed partner agency for a referral. Confirm the appointment and location before visiting.
resources.eligibility: Women seeking employment
resources.services: Professional clothing, career coaching
resources.notes: Employment clothing and career support. See the current referral agency list.

resources.name: Center for Work Education and Employment (CWEE)
resources.intake: Call 303-892-8444 to confirm eligibility, referral requirements, and the next orientation.
resources.eligibility: 18+, must be eligible to work in the U.S., meet income guidelines
resources.services: GED prep, employment coaching, career pathways
resources.notes: Ask your Colorado Works caseworker about a referral if enrolled.

resources.name: Division of Vocational Rehabilitation
resources.intake: Start through the state DVR website or call the main line for current office routing and application instructions.
resources.eligibility: Disability that creates a barrier to employment; vocational rehabilitation services needed to prepare for, obtain or retain work. DVR determines eligibility.
resources.services: Individualized employment planning and support to prepare for, obtain and retain employment.
resources.notes: Prior Hampden address and direct number were not reverified.

resources.name: Goodwill of Colorado
resources.intake: Use Career Development Services to find a program. For CW STEP, ask your Colorado Works caseworker about a referral.
resources.eligibility: People facing barriers to employment; program-specific screening. CW STEP requires active Colorado Works/TANF benefits and caseworker referral.
resources.services: Career matching, skills training, resume/interview preparation, job readiness support and mentoring.
resources.notes: Confirm assigned location and program eligibility before traveling.

resources.name: ReHire Colorado
resources.intake: Confirm current Denver contractor and open enrollment before referring.
resources.eligibility: Colorado resident age 18+; lawfully present and eligible to work; available for employment and not incarcerated; family income below 150% of federal poverty level; unemployed or working no more than 20 hours/week for four consecutive weeks; active public workforce job search. Confirm current contractor screening.
resources.services: Transitional paid employment, job skills assessment/training, coaching, job placement and ongoing support.
resources.notes: State budget documentation references ReHire. Current local intake was not verified.

resources.name: Denver Workforce Center (DEDO)
resources.intake: Call 720-337-9675 or email workforce@denvergov.org. Check the city’s current center locations and hours before visiting.
resources.eligibility: Jobseekers, including youth, older adults, veterans, newcomers and people with disabilities; ask about specific training eligibility.
resources.services: No-cost career coaching, job search and resume help, training connections, computer/internet access and employment support.
resources.notes: Use the main workforce contact for career coaching, job search, or training referrals.

resources.name: Colorado Coalition for the Homeless – Vocational Services
resources.intake: Call Vocational Services at 303-312-9835 to ask about intake, eligibility, and appointment location.
resources.eligibility: Employment help for jobseekers; specialized services for veterans, women and people experiencing homelessness. Call for program eligibility assessment.
resources.services: Individual employment plans, career counseling, resume/interview help, readiness training, job search/placement and ongoing support.
resources.notes: Ask about job coaching, training, work clothing, and other employment barriers.

resources.name: Denver SNAP to Success
resources.intake: Ask your SNAP eligibility technician for screening or call Denver Human Services at 720-944-4347.
resources.eligibility: Denver SNAP participants. Ask about program eligibility and referral.
resources.services: Job coaching, resume building, interview prep, employer connections
resources.notes: For general job assistance, see Denver Workforce Development.

resources.name: St. Francis Center Employment Services
resources.hours: Orientation Tue and Thu at 9 AM at the Day Center.
resources.intake: Attend the required orientation at the St. Francis Center Day Center. Call to confirm schedule and fit before visiting.
resources.eligibility: Justice-involved individuals
resources.services: Job search support, resume help, bus tokens, work tools/boots
resources.notes: Orientation is at the Day Center, not the employment office.

resources.name: We Don’t Waste – Mobile Food Markets
resources.hours: Varies by market. Check the live calendar.
resources.intake: Choose a location and reserve a time through Plentiful before going.
resources.eligibility: Open to everyone. No ID or proof of income required.
resources.services: Free groceries at rotating mobile market sites.
resources.notes: Use the market address in the reservation. The East 39th Avenue address is the organization’s office. Food audit 2026-11-23: https://www.wedontwaste.org/what-we-do/mobile-markets/

resources.name: Re:Vision – No-Cost Grocery
resources.intake: Walk in at the Re:Vision Gallery. No appointment needed.
resources.eligibility: All are welcome.
resources.services: No-cost grocery, urban agriculture, promotora leadership, community education
resources.notes: Food justice nonprofit empowering residents through food and leadership Food audit 2026-11-23: https://www.revision.coop/no-cost-grocery-program

resources.name: The Action Center
resources.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9–11:30 AM and 1–3:30 PM
resources.intake: Book a Food Market appointment online. A limited same-day lottery starts at 8:40 AM or 12:40 PM. Arrive no earlier than 8:30 AM or 12:30 PM.
resources.eligibility: Free groceries for households needing food.
resources.services: Clothing assistance, emergency support
resources.notes: An appointment or a same-day lottery spot is needed. Check the provider page for closures. Food audit 2026-11-23: https://www.theactioncenter.org/food-market

resources.name: Bienvenidos Food Bank
resources.hours: Jan-Oct: 1st, 2nd and 4th Thursdays, 10 am-noon and 3:30-5:30 pm. Nov-Dec: 1st, 2nd and 3rd Thursdays, same hours. Check closure notices.
resources.intake: Drop-in registration; arrive at least 10 minutes before closing. Bring reusable bags/box, name/phone and ID or address proof if available.

Through our Housing Now program, we are able to provide short term rental assistance to people in need, as well as case management, resources, and home visits.
More Than Financial Assistance
Our program partners with families experiencing homelessness by helping them to transition into long-term and stable housing by providing them with housing navigation, short term financial assistance, resources, and case management. We also partner with the community to provide friendship, financial literacy, and working towards long-term goals.

resources.intake: Call 303-602-8986 to be screened. If you lack stable housing, ask how visits can be arranged.
resources.eligibility: Eligible first-time pregnant parents. Denver Health screens for program requirements.
resources.services: Free nurse support during pregnancy and after birth for eligible participants.
resources.notes: Confirm intake and service availability directly.

resources.name: Colorado LEAP – Denver Heating Assistance
resources.hours: Seasonal. Check the current application window.
resources.intake: Follow the Denver LEAP page to apply or call 866-432-8435 for help. Gather income information and a heating bill, or ask what to supply if heat is included in rent.
resources.eligibility: Eligible Denver households responsible for home heating costs. Income and program requirements apply.
resources.services: Seasonal assistance with part of home heating costs.
resources.notes: Denver listed the 2026–27 season as open when checked.

resources.name: Energy Outreach Colorado – Bill Payment Assistance
resources.intake: Use the program page to locate a partner agency. Contact the agency to confirm eligibility, documents, and available funds before applying.
resources.eligibility: Colorado households needing help with heating or electric bills. Partner screening applies.
resources.services: Heating and electric bill payment assistance through local agencies.
resources.notes: The provider also encourages applicants to apply for LEAP when eligible.

resources.name: Denver Temporary Rental and Utility Assistance (TRUA)
resources.hours: Applications open in scheduled windows. Check the portal for current status.
resources.intake: Apply through the TRUA portal when it opens. Have a current demand for rent or documentation of an active eviction case. For a filed eviction, also see the Denver eviction clinics under Legal Aid Resources.
resources.eligibility: Denver renters with a current demand for rent or active eviction case. Program screening and funding apply.
resources.services: Temporary rental, utility, or relocation assistance for eligible households.
resources.notes: The portal was closed when checked on November 23, 2026. It listed December 15, 2026 as the next scheduled opening. Check for changes. City guidance: [Denver rental assistance guidance](https://denvergov.org/RentHelp)

resources.name: St. Francis Center – Clothing Room
resources.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 10–11 AM and 2–3 PM; Wed 10–11 AM and noon–1 PM (third Wed 10 AM–noon); Sat–Sun 10–11 AM and 1–2 PM.
resources.intake: Visit the day center during clothing-room hours. Call to confirm closures or availability.
resources.eligibility: Day center guests seeking clothing or shoes.
resources.services: Access to clean clothing, shoes, and accessories.
resources.notes: For urgent clothing needs, Denver County residents can also ask the Denver Human Services GIVE Center about assistance. See the GIVE Center listing under ID & Vital Documents.

resources.name: Denver Rescue Mission – Furniture Distribution
resources.intake: Case managers at approved organizations can request furniture for clients. Call to confirm agency approval, request screening, and pickup arrangements.
resources.eligibility: Clients referred by case managers at approved organizations.
resources.services: Furniture distribution by approved agency referral, subject to screening and availability.
resources.notes: Confirm arrangements before traveling.

resources.name: Sleepwell – Furniture Support for Recovery
resources.intake: Use the furniture request option on the website. Confirm availability and pickup or delivery arrangements directly.
resources.eligibility: People in recovery in the Denver metro area. Confirm program fit directly.
resources.services: Donated furniture support for people in recovery.
resources.notes: Confirm arrangements before traveling.

resources.name: St. Francis Center – Mail & Storage
resources.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 8 AM–2 PM; Wed 8 AM–1 PM (third Wed closes at noon); Sat–Sun 8 AM–noon.
resources.intake: Ask day center staff how to set up mail service. Call or visit during service hours to ask about storage, available space, and limits.
resources.eligibility: Day center guests seeking mail or belongings storage. Confirm registration and storage availability.
resources.services: Mail services and limited belongings storage.
resources.notes: Confirm mailing instructions with staff before sending mail.

resources.name: Denver Health – RED Primary Care Clinic
resources.intake: Call Linkage to Care at 303-602-3652 for new-patient or re-entry assistance. Established patients call 303-602-6443. Confirm appointment location.
resources.eligibility: People living with HIV seeking primary care or reconnecting to care.
resources.services: HIV primary care and linkage to treatment and support.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and eligibility with the provider.

resources.name: Denver Sexual Health Clinic
resources.intake: Call to schedule or use the clinic page. Confirm appointment location and ask about cost.
resources.eligibility: People seeking HIV or STI testing or evaluation.
resources.services: HIV and STI testing and sexual health services by appointment.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and eligibility with the provider.

resources.name: Colorado Health Network – Health Access Program
resources.intake: Call the Denver office and ask for Health Access. Review the application requirements. For a paper SDAP application, call 303-692-2716.
resources.eligibility: Eligible Coloradans living with HIV or seeking financial assistance for PrEP. Program-specific screening applies.
resources.services: Help accessing eligible medications, insurance premiums, and related costs through SDAP or the separate PrEP assistance program.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and eligibility with the provider.

resources.name: Denver Community Fridges – Re:Vision Site
resources.intake: Walk up and take food as available. No appointment needed.
resources.eligibility: Open to the public.
resources.services: Free food from a community fridge and pantry, as stocked.
resources.notes: The scheduled Re:Vision grocery pantry operates separately at 3738 Morrison Rd.

resources.name: Aurora Regional Navigation Campus – Overnight Shelter
resources.hours: Overnight. Call for current arrival instructions.
resources.intake: Call Advance Pathways to confirm Tier 1 intake, arrival instructions, and bed availability.
resources.eligibility: Adults 18+ experiencing homelessness. Families with children should ask for a family shelter referral.
resources.services: Low-barrier overnight shelter, meals, and access to support services.
resources.notes: Check current availability before traveling.

resources.name: Comitis Crisis Center – Emergency Family Shelter
resources.hours: Call for current intake and availability.
resources.intake: Call before traveling to confirm family shelter intake, screening, and where to go.
resources.eligibility: Families experiencing homelessness. Confirm eligibility directly.
resources.services: Emergency family shelter and support.
resources.notes: Check current availability before traveling.

resources.name: Denver Severe Weather Shelter
resources.hours: Available during city activations. Check current status.
resources.intake: Check Denver Find Shelter for active sites, hours, and instructions. Use the designated intake location for your household.
resources.eligibility: People needing shelter during a severe weather activation. Site access varies.
resources.services: City updates on emergency shelter and warming options.
resources.notes: Check current availability before traveling.

resources.name: Urban Peak – Youth Overnight Shelter
resources.hours: Shelter operates 24/7. Call for intake and waitlist timing.
resources.intake: Call the shelter directly at 303-974-2908 to ask about intake and the waitlist before traveling.
resources.eligibility: Youth ages 12–24 experiencing homelessness.
resources.services: Emergency youth shelter. See Urban Peak under Youth & Teen Services for daytime drop-in support.
resources.notes: Check current availability before traveling.

resources.name: Christ’s Body Ministries – Daily Bread
resources.intake: Visit during published breakfast hours. Call to confirm holiday schedule.
resources.eligibility: People seeking a prepared breakfast.
resources.services: Hot breakfast and coffee.
resources.notes: Check current provider hours before traveling.

resources.name: SAME – No Cost Grocery Market
resources.intake: Visit the grocery market during posted hours. Confirm holiday changes on the provider page.
resources.eligibility: Neighbors experiencing barriers to food access.
resources.services: Free groceries at the market. SAME Café lunch operates separately at 2023 E. Colfax Ave.
resources.notes: Check current provider hours before traveling.

resources.name: Denver Rescue Mission – Ministry Outreach Center Food Pantry
resources.intake: Check pantry instructions before going and bring valid photo ID. Ask about alternatives if you lack photo ID.
resources.eligibility: Households needing food. Provider lists pickup once per month.
resources.services: Monthly food pantry pickup and hygiene supplies when available.
resources.notes: Check current provider hours before traveling.

resources.name: Colorado Coalition for the Homeless – Health Outreach Program
resources.intake: Call 720-508-8268 or email HOPCoordinators@coloradocoalition.org to confirm the next stop, hours, and available services. New patients can walk in at scheduled stops.
resources.eligibility: People who need care through the mobile clinic, including new patients.
resources.services: Mobile primary care, including pediatric care, pharmacy services, and specialty referrals.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and availability with the provider.

resources.name: Colorado Coalition for the Homeless – Street Medicine
resources.hours: Field outreach. Contact the team for availability.
resources.intake: Email streetmedicine@coloradocoalition.org to ask about outreach, service area, and how to connect someone with the team.
resources.eligibility: People experiencing unsheltered homelessness, including people living in vehicles or encampments.
resources.services: Medical care in the community and coordination with Coalition clinics and outreach teams.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and availability with the provider.

resources.name: DAWN Clinic – Aurora
resources.intake: Call 303-800-9677 or use the clinic contact form to request an appointment. If you have no fixed address, ask how the clinic confirms Aurora residency.
resources.eligibility: Uninsured adults age 18 and older who live in Aurora.
resources.services: Free clinic care for eligible uninsured adults.
resources.notes: Confirm current access and availability with the provider.

resources.name: Rocky Mountain Human Services – Long-Term Services and Supports Assessment
resources.intake: Call the Case Management Agency or submit an online referral. Individuals, families, and providers can refer. Ask how to obtain the Professional Medical Information Page (PMIP) for the assessment.
resources.eligibility: People in Denver or Adams County seeking long-term care. Program and Medicaid eligibility are assessed separately.
resources.services: Medicaid long-term care assessment and referral guidance for nursing facility care and Medicaid-certified assisted living (Alternative Care Facilities).
resources.notes: For assisted living, ask the facility about room and board charges.

resources.name: Sobriety House – Residential Treatment
resources.intake: Call admissions for a pre-screening. Ask about availability, coverage, and any waitlist check-in requirements.
resources.eligibility: Adults seeking substance use treatment, subject to admissions screening. Colorado Medicaid is accepted for eligible services.
resources.services: Intensive residential and transitional residential substance use treatment.

resources.name: Colorado Mental Health Transitional Living Homes
resources.intake: Use the state program page to contact the Admissions and Coordination team for the Level 1 or Level 2 referral packet and required clinical records. Colorado organizations can submit referrals.
resources.eligibility: Colorado adults with serious mental illness who meet the applicable placement criteria, subject to review.
resources.services: Residential mental health support with different levels of supervision and clinical services.
resources.notes: The state prioritizes people awaiting step-down placement from state mental health hospitals.

resources.name: Behavioral Health Solutions Center (BHSC)
resources.intake: No public walk-ins. Admission is through first responders and approved mental health organizations. Outreach staff should use their agency’s approved referral process.
resources.eligibility: Adults experiencing a behavioral health crisis, subject to referral and screening.
resources.services: Voluntary short-term crisis stabilization for adults, with temporary shelter for eligible participants.
resources.notes: For public walk-in crisis assessment, go to WellPower’s 24/7 Walk-In Crisis Center at 4353 E. Colfax Ave., Denver. No appointment or insurance is required. [WellPower walk-in crisis services](https://www.wellpower.org/crisis-services/)

resources.name: Open Arms Assisted Living
resources.intake: Call admissions before arranging transport. Ask about Medicaid openings, referrals from street or shelter outreach, and whether screening can start while Medicaid is pending.
resources.eligibility: Admission depends on the facility assessment, care needs, and availability.
resources.services: Assisted living in Montbello. The provider lists Medicaid beds and has identified people at risk of homelessness as a priority.
resources.notes: Ask admissions about room and board costs.

resources.name: Dayspring Villa – Assisted Living
resources.intake: Call admissions before arranging transport. Ask about Medicaid openings, referrals from street or shelter outreach, and whether screening can start while Medicaid is pending.
resources.eligibility: Admission depends on the facility assessment, care needs, and availability.
resources.services: Assisted living for older adults. The provider accepts Medicaid.
resources.notes: Ask admissions about room and board costs.

resources.name: SparkHope Automotive – Vehicle Repair Assistance
resources.services: Discounted vehicle repairs and maintenance through the SHIFT program.
resources.eligibility: Eligible single mothers in Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, or Jefferson County. Review the application for work and vehicle requirements.
resources.intake: Apply online for SHIFT. Ask about eligibility and your share of repair costs before scheduling work.
resources.notes: Formerly Hands of The Carpenter. SHIFT participants pay 50% of the retail labor rate.

resources.name: Colorado DMV – Emissions Waivers
resources.services: Registration help after a failed emissions test through economic hardship, repair, or diagnostic waivers.
resources.eligibility: Requirements vary by waiver. The economic hardship waiver is for eligible gasoline vehicles and can be issued once per vehicle.
resources.intake: Review the DMV requirements and use the application instructions for your waiver type. If you have a metal plate, start at myDMV under Vehicle Services.
resources.notes: A waiver can help with registration. It does not pay for repairs.

resources.name: Colorado Coalition for the Homeless – Native American Services
resources.intake: Contact the Native American Services team using the program page for current intake.
resources.eligibility: Native American and Indigenous community members experiencing homelessness or housing instability. Confirm program eligibility.
resources.services: Housing navigation, help obtaining vital documents, and connections to care and benefits.
resources.notes: The team provides navigation and referrals. Emergency shelter placements and motel vouchers are handled elsewhere.

resources.name: Denver Indian Family Resource Center – Resource & Referral
resources.intake: Call and ask for Resource & Referral.
resources.eligibility: People who self-identify as American Indian or Alaska Native.
resources.services: Connections to housing, utility assistance, clothing, and legal referrals.

resources.name: Servicios de La Raza – Essential Community Support
resources.intake: Call for the current pantry schedule and how to access food or other essentials.
resources.eligibility: Contact the program for any requirements for the service you need.
resources.services: Food assistance and other essentials through a culturally responsive community program.

resources.name: Mile High WorkShop – Second Chance Employment
resources.services: Paid transitional employment, production and manufacturing skills training, coaching, and support finding the next job.
resources.intake: Submit the program interest form. Confirm current recruiting dates and schedule.
resources.eligibility: People facing barriers to employment, including people with criminal records. Ask about participation requirements.

resources.notes: Program eligibility FAQ: [CrossPurpose program eligibility FAQ](https://crosspurpose.org/programs/faq/)
resources.name: CrossPurpose – Leader Career Training
resources.services: Free in-person career training and job preparation.
resources.intake: Apply online for the Leader program. Ask about requirements for the specific training track.
resources.eligibility: Previous justice involvement and current parole are allowed. Applicants with an open case must wait until it closes.

resources.name: Anthem Denver – Laundry Love
resources.services: Free washing and drying for clothes and bedding.
resources.intake: Go to Coin Laundry during the event and ask for Laundry Love volunteers.
resources.eligibility: People and families with low or no income.
resources.hours: First Saturday, 10 a.m.–noon. Check the organizer page before going.

resources.name: Denver Property Storage
resources.services: City instructions for reclaiming belongings collected during a Denver cleanup.
resources.intake: Use the city page or call 311 (720-913-1311 from outside Denver).
resources.eligibility: People seeking belongings collected during a city cleanup.

resources.name: Denver Human Services – GIVE Center Hygiene Supplies
resources.services: Free wellness and hygiene items, subject to availability.
resources.intake: Check the GIVE Center page for current access instructions and hours.
resources.eligibility: Denver County residents.

resources.name: Community Outreach Service Center (COSC) – Basic Needs & Navigation
resources.hours: Mon–Thu 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; Fri 9 a.m.–1 p.m.
resources.intake: Call or stop by the outreach center during office hours. Ask about the specific service or supplies you need.
resources.eligibility: People experiencing homelessness or financial hardship in the Denver metro area. Ask about requirements for individual programs.
resources.services: Clothing, hygiene kits, help with SNAP and identity documents, housing application navigation, and community referrals.
resources.notes: COSC refers people to the Agape Soul Food Pantry next door. Ask staff about the current schedule and availability.

resources.name: Spirit of the Sun – Indigenous Food Share
resources.intake: New requests are by referral only. Contact jojo@spiritofthesun.org to ask how to make a referral and confirm pickup or delivery.
resources.eligibility: Native and Indigenous community members.
resources.services: Free food boxes for Native and Indigenous community members.

resources.name: Colorado Black Health Collaborative – Barbershop & Salon Health Outreach
resources.intake: Call to confirm the next screening location and time before going.
resources.eligibility: Community outreach focused on Black and African American communities.
resources.services: Blood pressure screenings, health education, and referrals at participating barbershops and salons.

resources.name: Safehouse Progressive Alliance for Nonviolence (SPAN)
resources.intake: Call the 24-hour crisis line for support or to ask about shelter access.
resources.eligibility: Survivors of interpersonal violence in Boulder and Broomfield counties. Call to confirm shelter eligibility and availability.
resources.services: Confidential crisis support, safety planning, and emergency shelter screening. Services are free and available in English and Spanish.

resources.name: Aurora Mental Health & Recovery – Asian Pacific Clinic
resources.intake: Call for referral assistance or use the referral form linked on the clinic page. Ask about language access and whether health navigation is available for your needs.
resources.eligibility: Children, adults, and older adults from immigrant and refugee communities. Contact the clinic to confirm intake.
resources.services: Culturally and linguistically responsive counseling, psychiatric services, case management, and outreach and navigation.
resources.notes: For referrals, the clinic also lists ClinicReferrals@AuroraMHR.org.

resources.name: Village Exchange Center – Village Pantry
resources.hours: Denver lists Wednesdays, noon–4 p.m.; call to confirm.
resources.intake: Call before traveling to confirm pantry hours, registration, and whether an appointment is needed.
resources.eligibility: People seeking groceries; ask about current enrollment requirements.
resources.services: Community food pantry serving Aurora households, including immigrant and refugee communities.

resources.name: Justice and Mercy Legal Aid Center (JAMLAC) – Immigration Law
resources.intake: Review the cases listed and complete the online prequalification form.
resources.eligibility: Low-income applicants. Eligible case types depend on residence and whether the applicant is a victim. JAMLAC excludes asylum, deportation and detention cases and cases with a hearing in the next four weeks.
resources.services: Immigration legal screening for qualifying matters such as family petitions, naturalization, and DACA renewals.

resources.name: Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC) – Citizenship & DACA Guidance
resources.intake: Call or email legalservices@coloradoimmigrant.org for upcoming workshops or application guidance.
resources.eligibility: People seeking guidance on citizenship or DACA. Ask about workshop registration.
resources.services: Free workshops and application guidance. Staff can connect people to additional legal services; they do not provide attorney representation.

resources.name: WeeCycle – Mobile Baby Essentials
resources.services: Diapers, wipes, baby food, and formula at mobile distribution events, subject to availability.
resources.intake: Check the current distribution calendar for the next site and time. Use the partner directory on the same page for baby gear and other supplies.
resources.eligibility: Families who need baby essentials. WeeCycle asks for general household information at distribution.

resources.name: Catholic Charities of Denver – Head Start & Early Head Start
resources.services: Early childhood education and family support through Head Start and Early Head Start.
resources.intake: Use the Early Childhood Education page to contact the program about enrollment, available sites, and age requirements.
resources.eligibility: Families with young children, including families experiencing homelessness and children in foster care. Ask the program about eligibility and openings.
